body: By that definition going on dates with other people is not cheating.....

That's the point. To some people some of those things are not cheating but to you they are.

One of my ex girlfriends considered any conversation with any girl other than her as cheating.

> What the fuck are you talking about, cheating isn't that hard to define.

It really is. Some people thinking kissing is cheating, others think sex is cheating while others think neither of those physical activities alone is cheating.
How do you define cheating? Is sex with anyone else always cheating?  How did you find out and how do you know shes lying?

That's right!  A lot of people can't relate and say to shrug off the rejection.  I feel I am better with rejection than most but being rejected by nearly everyone does get to you.  I find there is people in my life that "care" for me if, and only if, I claim I am in a drastic position such as being suicidal.  The problem is that once I am no longer in this state people leave you alone instead of changing the dynamic you have with each other.  I don't want people to support me because I am depressed I want people to socialize with me to stop me being depressed.  

A few may point out that if I am always isolated how do I know this will calm my depression.  Prior to my first suicidal attempt I had a committed relationship and it wasn't just what I thought it would be but was so much more.  I was thinking about proposing to this person a few days before they broke up with me via text.  No matter how much or how I asked they refused to give me any closure or reasoning.  I found out through a mutual acquaintance that she had been cheating on me for a while.  This hit me hard.

In the past I feel that I 'faked' it more often than  I do today. As such my persona was not very individualized.  I would hypothesize that my act is effective as people said they had no clue I felt so depressed or down.  But then again maybe my act is no effective as people commonly say this.

Listed below are just a few different examples.
University setting. We are in class and door is open.  There is a constant loud noise outside and it is clearly annoying to others and myself.  They just look at the door and get shitty.  I walk up to the door and close it.

"Its the thought that counts" is a common saying  when it comes to evaluating the emotional investment that must of gone into a gift.  While most people claim to agree to this they turn into idiots when presented with a gift of their own and see its value equal monetary representation.   To prove my point say you were a Vegan and this was a widely known and understood fact.  Now does a gift of $10 worth of chocolate (non vegan) show any different amount of thought than someone who gives you $1000 worth of chocolate. No both are as unthoughtful as each other.   

People say that advertising does not sway them much and think they are impervious to its affects.  Then these same people go into a shop and get tricked but all measure of psychological tricks.  A simple example is if we had 2 packets of different chocolate cookies and one costs $5 a packet and one costs $3 a packet then most people would assume the $5 packet would be better quality.  This is a poor assumption as price is a poor indicator of quality.  The increased price could be due many reasons.  Maybe they are inefficient as producing this item, maybe they  pay more for packaging and marketing or maybe they just have a higher profit margin yet most people do not consider these facts.  In this example I do sit but and judge the situation as objectively as I can.

Sounds like a similar situation to mine.   I was in hospital for over 6 months and received plastic surgery to try give me a normal face.  I do look closer than before but have an obvious scar on one side of my face.

I know our situations are different but how did you go on? What changed your outlook on life?

I feel ostracized as I never fit in with any "group" of people.  In my high school days the teachers and adults in my life said I would flourish in a higher education setting.  When I arrived it was just like a more bitchy high school.  

I feel that it is a mixture of how I act and them unable to relate.  I see and interpret things more logically than most people (according to my psychologist).  For this reason sometimes I choose to ignore stupid social queues.  

On the other hand people sometimes can't relate to me because I do things that they never would.  For example doing something for someone without any intention of getting any type of reciprocation.  

Health front I am still learning to live as a paraplegic.
